packet.headline_seed: Trump and Xi are set to meet. Where do US-China tariffs stand?
packet.description_seed: The first US presidential visit to China in almost 10 years will test a fragile tariff truce.

what: Trump and Xi are set to meet. Where do US-China tariffs stand?

clean_source_blocks.text: The first US presidential visit to China in almost 10 years will test a fragile tariff truce.

Beijing has confirmed that US President Donald Trump will travel to China this week to meet Xi Jinping. The visit, from the 13 - 15 May, will be the first to China by a US president in nearly a decade - and comes at a pivotal moment for ties between the world's two largest economies. Executives from some of America's biggest companiess - including Boeing, Citigroup and Qualcomm - are expected to travel with Trump, potentially to make deals with Chinese firms. It will also mark a key test in the fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing. In April 2025, Trump unveiled sweeping import taxes on countries across the world, friend or foe.

U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in May 2026 during his first trip to China in eight years, as tensions between the world’s two largest economies continue to reshape global trade, technology, and energy markets. Since Trump returned to the White House in 2025, Washington and Beijing have engaged in an intense economic rivalry marked by tariffs, sanctions, export controls, and strategic negotiations. In May 2026, China invoked its anti-sanctions law in response to U.S. blacklisting measures targeting Chinese refineries accused of purchasing Iranian oil. Beijing warned domestic firms against complying with American sanctions, signaling a tougher stance against U.S. pressure.

The sweeping measures were a shock, especially for China, said policy researcher Ning Leng from Georgetown University. "It was the first time they dealt with Trump seriously, and they probably did not expect him to go ahead with it," Ning said. At the time, China was much more reliant on trade with America. The US was a key importer of Chinese manufactured goods, putting its workers at risk if American buyers turned away due to Trump's tariffs. The tensions added to existing issues that have weighed on China's economy for years, including sluggish domestic consumption, high unemployment and a prolonged property crisis. Exports to the US offered a lifeline for Chinese jobs, but with Trump, that was now put at risk.

A major effect of that policy was a tit-for-tat trade war between the US and China that saw them hit each other with tariffs that topped 100%. The tariffs were paused after Trump and Xi's last face-to-face meeting in South Korea in October. But threats from both sides have continued.

Trump won the 2016 election vowing to make trade fairer for the US and to bring manufacturing jobs back to the country.

In 2018, he had announced tariffs on $250bn (£185bn) of Chinese imports - the moment that many analysts say the trade war started.

The same year, Trump imposed levies on other trading partners - including Mexico, Canada and Europe - which he said were also taking advantage of the US.

The sweeping measures were a shock, especially for China, said policy researcher Ning Leng from Georgetown University.

"It was the first time they dealt with Trump seriously, and they probably did not expect him to go ahead with it," Ning said.

At the time, China was much more reliant on trade with America.

The US was a key importer of Chinese manufactured goods, putting its workers at risk if American buyers turned away due to Trump's tariffs.

The tensions added to existing issues that have weighed on China's economy for years, including sluggish domestic consumption, high unemployment and a prolonged property crisis.

Exports to the US offered a lifeline for Chinese jobs, but with Trump, that was now put at risk.

"It's harder for one country to withstand a trade war with another that it has trade surplus with," Ning said.

His administration chose to not lift Trump's tariffs on China, sharing a belief that the US needed to keep a lid on its rival's growth in sectors like technology, Ning said.

Next week, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping will meet in Beijing for a highly anticipated summit, the first of four potential meetings over the next year. It is unclear what the scope of discussion will be and what will come out of this meeting. But that is all well and good. The world is a safer place when its two largest economies and most powerful countries are on speaking terms. payload.title: Trumpin Kiinan-vierailu testaa hauraan tullirauhan
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain presidentin Donald Trumpin odotetaan tapaavan Kiinan presidentin Xi Jinpingin Pekingissä 13.–15. toukokuuta. Vierailu on ensimmäinen Yhdysvaltain presidentin Kiinan-matka lähes vuosikymmeneen ja osuu keskelle jännittynyttä kauppa- ja pakotekiistaa.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentin Donald Trumpin on määrä matkustaa Kiinaan tällä viikolla tapaamaan Kiinan presidentti Xi Jinpingiä. Pekingin vahvistaman vierailun odotetaan tapahtuvan 13.–15. toukokuuta, ja sen keskeiseksi koetinkiveksi nousee Washingtonin ja Pekingin hauras tullirauha.

## Ensimmäinen vierailu lähes vuosikymmeneen

Trumpin Kiinan-matka olisi ensimmäinen Yhdysvaltain presidentin vierailu maahan lähes kymmeneen vuoteen. Tapaaminen tulee aikaan, jolloin maailman kaksi suurinta taloutta ovat ajautuneet laajaan taloudelliseen vastakkainasetteluun.

Yhdysvaltain ja Kiinan suhteita ovat viime vuosina kiristäneet tullit, pakotteet, vientirajoitukset ja strategiset neuvottelut. Trump palasi Valkoiseen taloon vuonna 2025, minkä jälkeen Washingtonin linja Pekingiä kohtaan on pysynyt kovana. Huhtikuussa 2025 Trump julkisti laajoja tuontiveroja eri maiden tuotteille, myös Kiinalle.

Vierailulle odotetaan mukaan myös suurten yhdysvaltalaisyritysten johtajia. Mainittujen yhtiöiden joukossa ovat Boeing, Citigroup ja Qualcomm. Yritysjohtajien mukanaolo viittaa siihen, että matkan yhteydessä saatetaan valmistella tai edistää sopimuksia kiinalaisten toimijoiden kanssa.

## Tullit ja pakotteet painavat neuvotteluja

Tullikysymys on tapaamisen ytimessä, koska se vaikuttaa suoraan maiden väliseen kauppaan ja yritysten toimintaympäristöön. Kiina on ollut riippuvainen viennistä Yhdysvaltoihin, ja Yhdysvallat on ollut merkittävä kiinalaisten teollisuustuotteiden ostaja. Jos amerikkalaiset ostajat vähentävät hankintojaan tullien vuoksi, seuraukset voivat tuntua Kiinan teollisuudessa ja työpaikoissa.

Kiinan taloutta ovat samaan aikaan rasittaneet heikko kotimainen kulutus, korkea työttömyys ja pitkittynyt kiinteistökriisi. Tämän vuoksi vienti Yhdysvaltoihin on ollut monille kiinalaisille aloille tärkeä tukipilari.

Myös pakotekiista varjostaa tapaamista. Kiina on vedonnut pakotteiden vastaiseen lainsäädäntöönsä vastauksena Yhdysvaltain mustalle listalle lisäämiin kiinalaisiin jalostamoihin, joita Washington syyttää iranilaisen öljyn ostamisesta. Peking on varoittanut kotimaisia yrityksiä noudattamasta Yhdysvaltain pakotteita.

Georgetownin yliopiston tutkija Ning Lengin mukaan Trumpin aiemmat laajat tullitoimet tulivat Kiinalle yllätyksenä. Hänen arvionsa mukaan Peking ei aluksi odottanut Trumpin vievän toimia läpi. Nyt maiden johtajien tapaaminen näyttää, onko tullirauha kestävällä pohjalla vai jääkö se vain väliaikaiseksi hengähdystauoksi.
summary_bullets: Donald Trumpin odotetaan tapaavan Xi Jinpingin Kiinassa 13.–15. toukokuuta.
Vierailu on ensimmäinen Yhdysvaltain presidentin Kiinan-matka lähes vuosikymmeneen.
Tapaamisen keskiössä ovat tullit, pakotteet ja maiden hauras kaupparauha.

The first US presidential visit to China in almost 10 years will test a fragile tariff truce.

Beijing has confirmed that US President Donald Trump will travel to China this week to meet Xi Jinping. The visit, from the 13 - 15 May, will be the first to China by a US president in nearly a decade - and comes at a pivotal moment for ties between the world's two largest economies. Executives from some of America's biggest companiess - including Boeing, Citigroup and Qualcomm - are expected to travel with Trump, potentially to make deals with Chinese firms. It will also mark a key test in the fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing. In April 2025, Trump unveiled sweeping import taxes on countries across the world, friend or foe.

U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in May 2026 during his first trip to China in eight years, as tensions between the world’s two largest economies continue to reshape global trade, technology, and energy markets. Since Trump returned to the White House in 2025, Washington and Beijing have engaged in an intense economic rivalry marked by tariffs, sanctions, export controls, and strategic negotiations. In May 2026, China invoked its anti-sanctions law in response to U.S. blacklisting measures targeting Chinese refineries accused of purchasing Iranian oil. Beijing warned domestic firms against complying with American sanctions, signaling a tougher stance against U.S. pressure.

The sweeping measures were a shock, especially for China, said policy researcher Ning Leng from Georgetown University. "It was the first time they dealt with Trump seriously, and they probably did not expect him to go ahead with it," Ning said. At the time, China was much more reliant on trade with America. The US was a key importer of Chinese manufactured goods, putting its workers at risk if American buyers turned away due to Trump's tariffs. The tensions added to existing issues that have weighed on China's economy for years, including sluggish domestic consumption, high unemployment and a prolonged property crisis. Exports to the US offered a lifeline for Chinese jobs, but with Trump, that was now put at risk.
